```{r Step 1, Compute Wage Premium Measure, include=TRUE}
# ============================================================
# CPS INDUSTRY WAGE PREMIUM
# ============================================================

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Load cleaned wage-and-salary sample
# ------------------------------------------------------------

cps_wage_analysis <- read_csv(
  here(
    "01_tidydata",
    "IPUMS_CPS",
    "cps_wage_analysis_2000_2024.csv"
  )
)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Construct hourly earnings
# ------------------------------------------------------------

cps_wage_hourly <- cps_wage_analysis %>%
  filter(
    worker_type == "Wage and salary",
    wage_income_clean > 0,
    weeks_worked_clean > 0,
    usual_hours_clean >= 35,
    !is.na(asecwt_clean),
    !is.na(industry_clean),
    !is.na(years_schooling),
    !is.na(potential_experience)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    annual_hours =
      weeks_worked_clean * usual_hours_clean,

    hourly_wage =
      wage_income_clean / annual_hours,

    log_hourly_wage =
      log(hourly_wage)
  ) %>%
  filter(
    is.finite(hourly_wage),
    hourly_wage > 0,
    is.finite(log_hourly_wage)
  )


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Prepare regression variables
# ------------------------------------------------------------

cps_wage_hourly <- cps_wage_hourly %>%
  mutate(
    industry_factor = factor(industry_clean),
    education_factor = factor(educ_category),
    sex_factor = factor(sex),
    race_factor = factor(race),
    region_factor = factor(region),

    experience = potential_experience,
    experience_sq = potential_experience^2
  )


# ============================================================
# 4. Estimate pooled model with year × industry effects
# ============================================================

# The interaction between year and industry allows the
# industry wage premium to vary over time.

m_industry_wage <- feols(
  log_hourly_wage ~
    education_factor +
    experience +
    experience_sq +
    sex_factor +
    race_factor +
    region_factor |
    year^industry_factor,
  data = cps_wage_hourly,
  weights = ~asecwt_clean
)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Extract year × industry fixed effects
# ------------------------------------------------------------

industry_fe <- fixef(
  m_industry_wage
)$`year^industry_factor`


industry_wage_premium <- tibble(
  year_industry = names(industry_fe),
  industry_premium_raw = as.numeric(industry_fe)
)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. Separate year and industry identifiers
# ------------------------------------------------------------

industry_wage_premium <- industry_wage_premium %>%
  separate(
    year_industry,
    into = c("year", "industry"),
    sep = "_",
    convert = TRUE
  )


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 7. Save the raw industry premiums
# ------------------------------------------------------------

saveRDS(
  industry_wage_premium,
  here(
    "01_tidydata",
    "IPUMS_CPS",
    "CPS_IndustryWagePremium_Raw_2000_2024.rds"
  )
)

write_csv(
  industry_wage_premium,
  here(
    "01_tidydata",
    "IPUMS_CPS",
    "CPS_IndustryWagePremium_Raw_2000_2024.csv"
  )
)
```

```{r Step 3, Diagnostic Check on the Measure, include=TRUE}
etable(m_industry_wage)

head(industry_wage_premium, 20)

summary(industry_wage_premium$industry_premium_raw)

n_distinct(industry_wage_premium$year)

n_distinct(industry_wage_premium$industry)


industry_fe <- fixef(m_industry_wage)$`year^industry_factor` 

industry_wage_premium <- tibble( 
  year_industry = names(industry_fe), 
  industry_premium_raw = as.numeric(industry_fe) 
  )

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Parse year and industry from the FE names
# ------------------------------------------------------------

industry_wage_premium <- industry_wage_premium %>% 
  separate( 
    year_industry, into = c("year", "industry"), 
    sep = "_", remove = FALSE ) %>% 
  mutate( year = as.integer(year), 
          industry = as.character(industry) 
          )

# Inspect parsing
head(industry_wage_premium)
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Create weighted industry-year cell weights
# ------------------------------------------------------------

industry_weights <- cps_wage_hourly %>% 
  group_by(year, industry_clean) %>% 
  summarise( industry_year_weight = sum( 
    asecwt_clean, na.rm = TRUE ), 
    industry_year_n = n(), .groups = "drop" ) %>% 
  mutate( industry = as.character(industry_clean) ) %>% 
  select( year, industry, industry_year_weight, industry_year_n 
          )

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Merge weights onto the fixed effects
# ------------------------------------------------------------

industry_wage_premium <- industry_wage_premium %>% 
  left_join( 
    industry_weights, by = c("year", "industry") 
    )

# 5. Verify that the merge worked
industry_wage_premium %>% 
  summarise( 
    n_cells = n(), 
    n_missing_weights = sum( 
      is.na(industry_year_weight) 
      ), 
    pct_missing_weights = mean(is.na(industry_year_weight)) * 100 
    )

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Calculate weighted mean raw FE within each year
# ------------------------------------------------------------

year_weighted_means <- industry_wage_premium %>% 
  group_by(year) %>% 
  summarise( weighted_mean_raw_fe = weighted.mean( 
    industry_premium_raw, w = industry_year_weight, na.rm = TRUE ), 
    .groups = "drop" 
    )

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. Normalize each industry-year FE around the
#    weighted mean for that year
# ------------------------------------------------------------
industry_wage_premium <- industry_wage_premium %>% 
  left_join( 
    year_weighted_means, 
    by = "year" 
    ) %>% 
  mutate( 
    industry_wage_premium = 
      industry_premium_raw - weighted_mean_raw_fe 
    )

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 7. Convert log-point premium into percentage premium
# ------------------------------------------------------------

industry_wage_premium <- industry_wage_premium %>%
  mutate(
    industry_wage_premium_pct =
      100 * (exp(industry_wage_premium) - 1)
  )

# Inspect
industry_wage_premium %>%
  select(
    year,
    industry,
    industry_premium_raw,
    weighted_mean_raw_fe,
    industry_wage_premium,
    industry_wage_premium_pct
  ) %>%
  arrange(year, industry) %>%
  head(20)

# ============================================================
# Verify Within-Year Normalization
# ============================================================

normalization_check <- industry_wage_premium %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  summarise(
    weighted_mean_premium = weighted.mean(
      industry_wage_premium,
      w = industry_year_weight,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    min_premium = min(industry_wage_premium, na.rm = TRUE),
    max_premium = max(industry_wage_premium, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

normalization_check


#Cell Size Diagnostics
cell_size_summary <- industry_wage_premium %>% 
  summarise( 
    min_n = min(industry_year_n), 
    p1_n = quantile(industry_year_n, 0.01), 
    p5_n = quantile(industry_year_n, 0.05), 
    p10_n = quantile(industry_year_n, 0.10), 
    median_n = median(industry_year_n), 
    p90_n = quantile(industry_year_n, 0.90), 
    p95_n = quantile(industry_year_n, 0.95), 
    max_n = max(industry_year_n) ) 

cell_size_summary


industry_wage_premium %>% 
  summarise( 
    cells_total = n(), 
    cells_under_25 = sum(industry_year_n < 25), 
    cells_under_50 = sum(industry_year_n < 50), 
    cells_under_100 = sum(industry_year_n < 100), 
    cells_under_250 = sum(industry_year_n < 250), 
    cells_under_500 = sum(industry_year_n < 500) 
    )

small_cells <- industry_wage_premium %>% 
  arrange(industry_year_n) %>% 
  select( 
    year, 
    industry,
    industry_year_n, 
    industry_year_weight, 
    industry_wage_premium, 
    industry_wage_premium_pct 
    )

small_cells

head(small_cells, 25)

industry_wage_premium %>% 
  summarise( 
    correlation_n_premium = cor( 
      log(industry_year_n), 
      industry_wage_premium, use = "complete.obs" ), 
    correlation_n_abs_premium = cor( 
      log(industry_year_n), 
      abs(industry_wage_premium), use = "complete.obs" ) 
    )

cell_thresholds <- tibble( 
  threshold = c(5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 50, 75, 100, 150, 200) ) %>% 
  mutate( 
    cells_remaining = map_int( 
      threshold, ~ sum(industry_wage_premium$industry_year_n >= .x) 
      ), 
    cells_dropped = nrow(industry_wage_premium) - cells_remaining, 
    pct_cells_remaining = 100 * cells_remaining / nrow(industry_wage_premium), 
    pct_cells_dropped = 100 * cells_dropped / nrow(industry_wage_premium) 
    ) 

cell_thresholds



thresholds <- c(5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 50, 75, 100)

threshold_sample_impact <- map_dfr(
  thresholds,
  function(x) {

    keep <- industry_wage_premium$industry_year_n >= x

    tibble(
      minimum_n = x,

      cells_remaining = sum(keep),
      cells_dropped = sum(!keep),

      pct_cells_remaining =
        100 * mean(keep),

      weighted_sample_retained =
        sum(
          industry_wage_premium$industry_year_weight[keep],
          na.rm = TRUE
        ),

      pct_weighted_sample_retained =
        100 *
        sum(
          industry_wage_premium$industry_year_weight[keep],
          na.rm = TRUE
        ) /
        sum(
          industry_wage_premium$industry_year_weight,
          na.rm = TRUE
        )
    )
  }
)

threshold_sample_impact
# ============================================================
# Premium distribution under different cell-size thresholds
# ============================================================

premium_threshold_diagnostics <- map_dfr(
  c(1, 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 50, 100),
  function(x) {

    dat <- industry_wage_premium %>%
      filter(industry_year_n >= x)

    tibble(
      minimum_n = x,
      n_cells = nrow(dat),

      min_premium =
        min(dat$industry_wage_premium, na.rm = TRUE),

      p1_premium =
        quantile(
          dat$industry_wage_premium,
          0.01,
          na.rm = TRUE
        ),

      p5_premium =
        quantile(
          dat$industry_wage_premium,
          0.05,
          na.rm = TRUE
        ),

      median_premium =
        median(
          dat$industry_wage_premium,
          na.rm = TRUE
        ),

      p95_premium =
        quantile(
          dat$industry_wage_premium,
          0.95,
          na.rm = TRUE
        ),

      p99_premium =
        quantile(
          dat$industry_wage_premium,
          0.99,
          na.rm = TRUE
        ),

      max_premium =
        max(dat$industry_wage_premium, na.rm = TRUE)
    )
  }
)

premium_threshold_diagnostics

# ============================================================
# Compare observations retained/dropped at n >= 25
# ============================================================

industry_wage_premium %>%
  mutate(
    retained_n25 = industry_year_n >= 25
  ) %>%
  arrange(industry_wage_premium) %>%
  select(
    year,
    industry,
    industry_year_n,
    industry_year_weight,
    retained_n25,
    industry_wage_premium,
    industry_wage_premium_pct
  ) %>%
  head(30)

industry_wage_premium %>%
  mutate(
    retained_n25 = industry_year_n >= 25
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(industry_wage_premium)) %>%
  select(
    year,
    industry,
    industry_year_n,
    industry_year_weight,
    retained_n25,
    industry_wage_premium,
    industry_wage_premium_pct
  ) %>%
  head(30)



industry_wage_premium_final <- industry_wage_premium %>%
  filter(industry_year_n >= 25)

# Check number of retained cells
nrow(industry_wage_premium_final)

# Check year coverage
industry_wage_premium_final %>%
  count(year)
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Verify weighted normalization after the cell restriction
# ------------------------------------------------------------

final_normalization_check <- industry_wage_premium_final %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  summarise(
    weighted_mean_premium = weighted.mean(
      industry_wage_premium,
      w = industry_year_weight,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    weighted_sd_premium = sqrt(
      weighted.mean(
        (
          industry_wage_premium -
            weighted.mean(
              industry_wage_premium,
              w = industry_year_weight,
              na.rm = TRUE
            )
        )^2,
        w = industry_year_weight,
        na.rm = TRUE
      )
    ),
    min_premium = min(
      industry_wage_premium,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    max_premium = max(
      industry_wage_premium,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

final_normalization_check
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Check whether the retained sample still represents
#    essentially the full weighted labor force
# ------------------------------------------------------------

final_sample_coverage <- industry_wage_premium_final %>%
  summarise(
    retained_cells = n(),
    retained_weight =
      sum(industry_year_weight, na.rm = TRUE),
    total_weight =
      sum(
        industry_wage_premium$industry_year_weight,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),
    pct_weight_retained =
      100 * retained_weight / total_weight
  )

final_sample_coverage
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Final distribution of the continuous wage premium
# ------------------------------------------------------------

summary(
  industry_wage_premium_final$industry_wage_premium
)

summary(
  industry_wage_premium_final$industry_wage_premium_pct
)
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Identify the most extreme retained observations
# ------------------------------------------------------------

# Lowest premiums
industry_wage_premium_final %>%
  arrange(industry_wage_premium) %>%
  select(
    year,
    industry,
    industry_year_n,
    industry_year_weight,
    industry_wage_premium,
    industry_wage_premium_pct
  ) %>%
  head(20)


# Highest premiums
industry_wage_premium_final %>%
  arrange(desc(industry_wage_premium)) %>%
  select(
    year,
    industry,
    industry_year_n,
    industry_year_weight,
    industry_wage_premium,
    industry_wage_premium_pct
  ) %>%
  head(20)

write_csv(industry_wage_premium_final, here("01_tidydata", "IPUMS_CPS", "industry_wage_premium_2000_2025_n25.csv"))
```
